transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

I guess… I’ve been having a little trouble explaining myself clearly. It’s probably not as bad as I’m making it sound, but at work, someone will ask me something simple, like when a ring repair will be ready, and my answer starts wandering from invoices to garden soil to mortgage papers. And I can see their face change, like I’ve lost them. I thought maybe I should ask someone about it.
When you're trying to explain something, do your thoughts feel disorganized or jumbled inside your head, making it hard to stay on track?

Yes… I think so. Not all the time, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but sometimes when I’m trying to answer something simple, it doesn’t stay in a straight line. Like at work, someone asks when a ring repair will be done, and I start with that, but then I’m suddenly talking about invoices, or garden soil, or mortgage papers. I can tell from their face that I’m not making sense the way I meant to. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being inserted into your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being taken out or broadcasted to others?

Not exactly like… thoughts being put in or taken out, no. That sounds a little stronger than what I mean.

I have had this feeling—maybe I’m being silly—but I get convinced sometimes that certain customers are coming in to sort of check on me, like to see if I’m going to miss payments on the new showroom. They’ll ask a lot of questions about it, and my husband says they’re just being friendly, and maybe he’s right. But in the moment it feels like they’re asking for a reason. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel like people are talking about you or that their actions are directed at you, even if they don’t say it outright?

Yes… sometimes. I feel a little embarrassed saying it, because I know it might sound odd. But with some customers, when they ask a lot about the new showroom, I start feeling like they’re not just making conversation — like maybe they’re checking whether I’m going to miss payments or something. My husband says they’re probably just being friendly, and I try to believe that, but in the moment it really feels directed at me. Does that make sense?
Do you ever feel like people are acting in a certain way toward you, like they’re watching you or trying to send you a message, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but sometimes with customers, especially when they ask a lot about the new showroom, I start feeling like they’re not just being polite.

Like… I’ll get convinced they’re checking on whether I’m going to miss payments or something, because they keep asking questions. My husband tells me they’re probably just being friendly, and I try to take that in, but in the moment it feels like there’s a reason behind it. Does that count as what you mean?
Do you ever feel like things happening around you—like something on TV, a song playing, or something someone says—are meant specifically for you, even if they don’t seem connected at first?

Not so much with TV or songs, I don’t think. It’s more… things people say in person, like customers asking about the new showroom.

I know it sounds odd, and maybe I’m reading too much into it, but I’ve gotten convinced sometimes that they’re coming in to check whether I’m going to miss payments, because they ask so many questions. My husband tells me they’re just being friendly, and I try to accept that, but in the moment it feels like it’s meant for me somehow. Is that what you mean?

Have you ever felt that certain things happening around you—like something someone said, a sound, or even events in the news—were directly connected to you in a hidden or special way, even if others wouldn’t see the connection?

Yes… kind of. I mean, not really with the news or anything like that. It’s more when people are right there in front of me.

Like I said, with some customers asking so many questions about the new showroom, I start to feel like there’s something behind it… like they’re really there to see if I’m going to miss payments or if things are going badly. I know that probably sounds strange, and my husband tells me they’re just being friendly or curious. I try to believe him, I really do. But in the moment, it feels connected to me in that way. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?

Have you ever felt that random events, like something you saw on the street, a comment from a stranger, or even something in the environment like a noise or a sign, was meant to send you a message or had a special meaning just for you?

I don’t think it’s like signs or noises exactly… not that I can think of. It’s more with people, especially customers.

I know it probably sounds odd, and I’m not trying to make a big deal out of it, but when they ask a lot about the new showroom, I can get this feeling that they’re really checking on me—like whether I’m going to miss payments or if things aren’t going well. My husband says they’re just being friendly, and I try to listen to that. But in the moment it can feel like their questions mean something more. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being influenced by something or someone outside of yourself, like your mind isn’t fully your own?

I don’t think it’s like my thoughts are being controlled, exactly. That sounds stronger than what I mean.

It’s more that I can get really convinced about something, even when my husband tells me I’m probably taking it the wrong way. Like with customers asking so many questions about the new showroom… I start thinking they’re really there to see if I’m going to miss payments or if something’s wrong. I know that may sound odd, and I don’t want to overstate it, but in the moment it feels very real to me. Is that along the lines of what you mean?
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are not your own, like someone else can hear them or that they are being put into your mind?

No… I don’t think so. I’ve never felt like someone could hear my thoughts, or like thoughts were being put into my head.

I mean, I do get worked up about what people might mean sometimes, but my thoughts still feel like mine. I don’t want to answer it wrong, but for that specific thing, I don’t think that’s happened.
Have these beliefs about customers checking on you or sending you messages felt completely true to you, even when others, like your husband, have given you reasons to doubt them?

Yes… I guess in those moments it does feel true to me. I don’t want to sound unreasonable, because I know my husband may be right that they’re just being friendly, but when customers keep asking about the new showroom, I can get really convinced they’re checking on whether I’m going to miss payments or if something’s wrong.

Afterward I can see maybe I read too much into it, but at the time it feels hard to shake. Is that what you mean?

Have there been times when, despite knowing logically that your husband’s explanation made sense, you still couldn’t shake the feeling that the customers’ questions were about something more serious, like checking on our finances?

Yes… that’s probably fair to say. I know my husband’s explanation makes sense, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but even knowing that, I still get this feeling I can’t quite let go of.

Like when they ask a lot about the new showroom, I start thinking, why are they asking so much? Are they trying to see if we’re in trouble or if I’m going to miss payments? I know that sounds odd, and maybe I’m reading too much into it, but in the moment it feels serious to me.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that others might find extremely strange or impossible, even if they make sense to you?

I mean… not impossible, exactly. I don’t think I’ve had anything really bizarre like that.

But I know it probably sounds odd — I have gotten pretty convinced that some customers are coming in to check whether I’m going to miss payments or if something is wrong with the business. It’s mostly when they keep asking questions about the new showroom. My husband says they’re just being friendly or curious, and I know that makes sense, but in the moment it can feel like there’s more behind it.

I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.

Have there been times when you were completely sure about something—like customers checking on your finances—even when there was strong evidence that it wasn’t true or when others showed you it didn’t make sense?

Yes… I think there have been times like that, though I don’t like saying “completely sure” because I know how it sounds.

But with some customers, when they ask too many questions about the new showroom, I’ve gotten really convinced they’re coming in to check whether I’ll miss payments or whether something is wrong financially. My husband will tell me they’re probably just being friendly or curious, and I can understand that logically… but in the moment I still feel like there’s something more behind it.

I’m not trying to be difficult. It just feels very real at the time.

Have there been times when you remained completely convinced about something—like customers checking on your finances—even after seeing clear evidence that it wasn’t true or after others explained it didn’t make sense?

Yes… I think so, at least at the time. I don’t want to overstate it, because later I can sometimes see what my husband means.

But when certain customers keep asking about the new showroom, I’ve gotten really stuck on the idea that they’re checking whether I’m going to miss payments or if the business is in trouble. Even after my husband explains that they’re probably just being friendly, it doesn’t always settle it for me right away.

I know that may not make a lot of sense. I’m trying to answer honestly.
